explanations: terra: Earth is made a bed, sky a structure, and rain produces fruits; this is the same heaven-earth house and cultivated provision that the section sets before the soul.
terra: After mentioning what is on earth, the ayah turns to heaven and "فَسَوَّاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ"; it directly joins earth, built heavens, and creative taswiya as the source section does.

luna: Water bursts from the rock into springs (فَانْفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا); this is the water-gushing branch of the section's f-j-r meeting. | terra: The stone's water "فَانفَجَرَتْ" joins the source section's bursting-water sense of f-j-r to an apportioned drink, since every people knows its drinking place; rupture and measured water meet in one scene.
terra: Some stones have rivers burst from them and others split so water comes out; these two concrete openings preserve the water-breaking sense from which the section reads moral fujur.
terra: Abraham asks God to "وَابْعَثْ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا" who will purify them; divine sending and cultivation of the soul stand together, unlike the self-dispatch of 91:12.

luna: Turning back on one's heels (يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ) is a literal heel-branch in a passage about following or turning from the Messenger; it extends the section's heel/aftermath association into a different, directional sense.
terra: Fasting is prescribed "لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ"; bodily abstention makes the restraining sense of taqwa concrete.

luna: The fast ends at dawn, distinguished from night by the white thread of daybreak; the boundary between covering night and opened day is explicit here. | terra: The fasting ayah calls spouses garments for one another, sets a night-time boundary, and ends "لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ"; covering and restraint thus meet within one legal scene.
terra: A response to aggression must equal the aggression, and the command to practice taqwa follows; restraint and measured return stand together as in the water-share and punishment meeting.
luna: The one who spreads corruption on earth destroys crops and livestock (وَيُهْلِكَ الْحَرْثَ وَالنَّسْلَ); this is a close reversal of fruitful ground and animal provision under a transgressor.
terra: God "بَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ" as bearers of good news and warning; the explicit divine agent supplies the contrast to the unbidden self-rising of 91:12.
terra: A rainstorm leaves a thin-soiled rock bare, turning an outwardly fertile surface into sterility; it is the ruined moral field opposite genuine cultivation.
terra: Those seeking God's pleasure are like a high garden whose rain doubles its yield; beside 2:264 it supplies the section's two inward fields and their unlike harvests.
terra: Like Pharaoh's people and those before them, deniers are seized "بِذُنُوبِهِمْ"; it supports the section's claim that the return follows the deed.
terra: People are told to travel through the earth and see the deniers' outcome; ruined lands make ʿaqiba a visible trace behind communal denial.

luna: The phrase “turn back on your heels” (انْقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَىٰ أَعْقَابِكُمْ) uses the literal heel-branch related to the section's ʿuqbā, but here it means apostasy rather than a later consequence; it makes the bodily-root association a deliberate change of sense.

luna: The verse says God sent (بَعَثَ) a messenger among the believers; that same sending action clarifies the section's contrast between God's sent messenger and the man who raises himself. | terra: God "بَعَثَ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا" who recites and purifies them; this joins the section's contrast between a messenger whom God raises and the culprit who raises himself, while also meeting the soul's tazkiya.
terra: The disobedient wish "لَوْ تُسَوَّىٰ بِهِمُ الْأَرْضُ"; taswiya here means being leveled with the ground, the destructive pole paired in the section with forming sky and soul.

terra: The ayah forbids violating sacred signs and aggression, then pairs cooperation in righteousness and taqwa against sin and transgression; protected animal-boundaries and moral restraint meet explicitly.
terra: God "فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ غُرَابًا" to show Cain what to do; an animal is deliberately sent by God, sharply contrasting the section's man who launches himself like an unhobbling animal.
terra: A former people are destroyed "بِذُنُوبِهِمْ" after being established amid rain and rivers; their sin turns a flourishing water-built settlement into removal.
terra: The same travel command directs attention to the deniers' outcome, making destroyed places evidence of what followed their act.
terra: God takes people by night and "يَبْعَثُكُمْ فِيهِ" by day; daily raising is placed inside the night-day watch that the section transfers into the soul.

terra: God is "فَالِقُ الْحَبِّ وَالنَّوَىٰ," the splitter of grain and date-stone; the same kind of opening that yields life from a field clarifies the source section's meeting of inward breach, dawn, and cultivation.
terra: "فَالِقُ الْإِصْبَاحِ" makes dawn an opening, then places night, sun, and moon in a calculated order; it directly joins the section's torn darkness to the orderly cosmic watch.
terra: Many towns receive God's might by night or while resting at midday; communal judgment arrives within the same daily alternation that the section turns into a final watch.

luna: The verse names “the garment of God-consciousness” (وَلِبَاسُ التَّقْوَىٰ), directly matching the section's secondary image of taqwa as a protective covering. | terra: Ordinary clothing covers nakedness, then "لِبَاسُ التَّقْوَىٰ" is named the better garment; this directly supports the source section's developed sense of taqwa as a protective covering.

luna: This next verse says Satan strips the two people's garment (يَنْزِعُ عَنْهُمَا لِبَاسَهُمَا); beside the garment of taqwa in 7:26, it gives a specific image of a protective covering being torn away.
terra: Night covers day while pursuing it swiftly, and sun, moon, and stars remain subject to command; it restages the ordered cover-and-turn sequence carried into the soul.
terra: Good land brings vegetation abundantly, while bad land produces only scant growth; this is a Quranic two-field contrast closely matching the section's cultivated and buried soul-fields.

luna: Salih calls the she-camel God's sign and orders them to leave her grazing and not harm her; it gives the camel's divine ownership and protected share explicit form. | terra: Salih presents "نَاقَةُ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ آيَةً," orders that she graze God's earth, and forbids harm; this is the full divine-camel commission behind the compressed scene in surah 91.

luna: Thamud are settled in the land and take palaces from its plains (سُهُولِهَا قُصُورًا), directly grounding the section's plain, palaces, and their later leveling. | terra: Thamud make palaces "مِن سُهُولِهَا" and carve mountain houses; this is the section's exact plain-and-palace scene before the inhabited ground is ruined.
terra: The arrogant chiefs ask whether the oppressed know that Salih is sent by his Lord, explicitly placing divine sending inside the Thamud confrontation.
terra: The arrogant reject what Salih was sent with, supplying the refusal that moves from the divine mission of 7:75 to the camel's hamstringing in 7:77.

luna: The people hamstring the camel and defy their Lord's command (فَعَقَرُوا النَّاقَةَ وَعَتَوْا); this is the section's violation of the sign and its limit. | terra: They hamstring the camel, defy their Lord's command, and demand the threatened punishment; the deed is explicitly both bodily attack and broken boundary.

luna: The earthquake leaves them prostrate in their homes; this ayah supplies the bodily and domestic aftermath of the prior camel-killing. | terra: The quake seizes them and leaves them fallen in their dwelling, completing the bodily and architectural consequence of 7:77.
terra: Had the towns believed and practiced taqwa, blessings from sky and earth would have opened; this is the precise communal reversal of denial turning an ordered, fertile land into destruction.
terra: The towns are asked whether they feel secure from punishment coming by night while they sleep, making night-cover a possible closure of judgment.
terra: The paired warning asks whether punishment may come in morning brightness while they play; night and morning alike remain appointed turns under divine rule.
terra: Inheritors of ruined lands are warned that God could strike them for their sins; land and the consequence following ذنب meet directly.
terra: The earth belongs to God, who gives it to whom He wills, and "the outcome is for the muttaqin"; land, taqwa, and aftermath are joined in one promise.
terra: Pharaoh's people deny signs, so God destroys them "بِذُنُوبِهِمْ" and drowns them; sin, water, and communal consequence meet as they do in the section's Thamud reading.

luna: Charity is said to purify and cleanse (تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا); it offers a concrete act of tazkiya related to the section's purifying path, though the section does not name charity.
terra: God makes the sun radiance, the moon light, and measures its stations so years and reckoning can be known; this is the calculable heavenly order carried into moral measure by the section.
terra: The alternation of night and day and the creation of heavens and earth are signs; it joins the ordered watch of 10:5 to the whole built cosmos.

luna: After rain makes the earth's vegetation flourish, God's command comes by night or day and leaves it harvested (فَجَعَلْنَاهَا حَصِيدًا); this joins the section's crop and night-covering images in a sudden reversal. | terra: Worldly life is rain mingling with earth's growth until God's command comes by night or day and leaves it reaped; it unites water, flourishing field, severing, and the irreversible turn.
terra: After an unseen community story, the Prophet is told to be patient because "the outcome is for the muttaqin"; restraint governs what comes after.

luna: Salih says God brought the people forth from the earth (أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ); this links the messenger's address to the section's earth as the ground of human formation and Thamud's settlement. | terra: Salih tells Thamud that God produced them from earth and settled them in it; this makes their built, cultivated land a divine trust before they ruin it.

luna: Salih names the she-camel as God's sign, gives her grazing ground, and prohibits harm; it states the protected animal and boundary at the heart of the section. | terra: Salih names God's camel as a sign, lets her feed in God's earth, and warns against harm; the verse joins messenger, animal, pasture, and approaching consequence.

luna: After they hamstring her, Salih gives them three days before the promise is fulfilled; the ayah makes the consequence follow the act in time. | terra: After they hamstring her, their remaining enjoyment is measured as three days; the fixed term makes their own allotted aftermath answer the violated share.

luna: Salih and the believers who were with him are saved by mercy as the punishment arrives; this gives the section's two moral fields distinct outcomes. | terra: When God's command comes, Salih and the believers are saved while the wrongdoers are left for the blast; protection and communal consequence divide at the appointed turn.

luna: The cry seizes the wrongdoers in their homes, completing the earlier warning with the consequence that falls on the people who killed the camel. | terra: The blast seizes the wrongdoers and leaves them fallen in their homes, realizing the section's image of people and dwellings struck together.

luna: Their homes seem never to have been inhabited; the emptied settlement makes the section's leveled plain and vanished houses perceptible. | terra: They become as though they had never flourished in those homes; this erasure turns an inhabited built place into the section's barren aftermath.
terra: Lot is told that his people's fixed appointment is morning and that morning is near; the divinely fixed turn illustrates a judgment no human can delay or reverse.

luna: Joseph's speaker says the soul persistently urges evil (إِنَّ النَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ); this gives the section's inward fujūr a direct formulation. | terra: "إِنَّ النَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ" gives the soul an inward impulse toward evil unless shown mercy, clarifying how the inspired possibilities become a lived direction.
terra: God spreads earth, places stabilizers and paired fruits, then makes night cover day; this single ayah meets the section's spread ground, growth, and ordered covering.
terra: When God wills harm for a people, "فَلَا مَرَدَّ لَهُ"; this directly states the section's final claim that no later turn can repel the judgment.
terra: Valleys flow according to their measure while the torrent carries swelling foam that vanishes; this makes measured water bear an image of overflow and of what passes versus remains.
luna: The angels greet the steadfast with a good final outcome (فَنِعْمَ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ); this uses the section's ʿuqbā word-family for an outcome that contrasts with Thamud's irreversible end.
terra: The garden is "عُقْبَى الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوا" while the unbelievers' outcome is fire; this explicitly joins taqwa to its aftermath, unlike Thamud's ruin.
luna: A good word is compared to a firmly rooted tree whose branches reach the sky (كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ); this makes the section's two moral courses perceptible as different growth rooted within.
luna: The good tree bears its fruit at every season (تُؤْتِي أُكُلَهَا كُلَّ حِينٍ); this ayah contributes the productive outcome of the moral tree introduced just before it.

luna: The bad word is a tree uprooted from the earth without stability (كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ اجْتُثَّتْ); this completes the previous ayah's fruitful tree with a clear counterpart to the section's buried, unproductive field.
terra: God creates heavens and earth, sends water, brings fruit, and subjects ships and rivers; built cosmos, released water, and provision meet in one ayah.
terra: Sun and moon run constantly and night and day are subjected, completing the ordered creation-and-provision sequence of 14:32.
terra: God spreads the earth, anchors it, and grows in it "مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَّوْزُونٍ"; spread ground, cultivation, and measure meet exactly as in the section.
terra: God announces that after He has fashioned the human, "سَوَّيْتُهُ," and breathed spirit into him, the angels must bow; taswiya here is bodily and inward completion.
terra: The people of al-Hijr carve mountain houses while feeling secure, restaging the durable architecture whose apparent order cannot shield transgression.
terra: The blast takes them in the morning, placing judgment at a turn of night and day as the section's closing watch does.
terra: What they had earned does not avail them; this gives the carved houses of 15:82 no power to reverse the morning judgment of 15:83.
terra: Water descends from heaven as drink and as the source of vegetation where animals pasture, joining the section's water-share, field, and herd.
terra: The same rain grows crops, olives, palms, grapes, and fruits; it gives the cultivated result opposite the section's barren aftermath.
terra: Night, day, sun, moon, and stars are all subjected by command, setting the ordered cosmic watch immediately beside the watered field of 16:10-11.
luna: A destroyed people's roof falls in upon them (فَخَرَّ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّقْفُ); this parallels the section's palaces leveled with their inhabitants, though it speaks of another town.

luna: God says He sent (بَعَثْنَا) a messenger to every community, calling them to worship Him and avoid false gods; this states the divine sending side of the section's contrast with the man who launches himself into rebellion. | terra: God raises in every community a messenger, then commands the reader to see the deniers' outcome; divine baʿth and communal ʿaqiba meet in one ayah, just as the section joins them around Thamud.
terra: Garments "تَقِيكُمُ الْحَرَّ" and armor "تَقِيكُم بَأْسَكُمْ" physically shield and restrain harm, preserving the concrete protective sense behind the section's taqwa image.
terra: Retaliation must match what was suffered, using repeated ʿ-q-b forms; the bounded equivalence clarifies the source section's link between what comes after and a measured return.
terra: Night and day are two signs: the night sign is effaced and the day sign made visible so time can be counted; covering, opening, and calculation meet explicitly.

luna: God gives Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wrong her (ءَاتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ النَّاقَةَ مُبْصِرَةً فَظَلَمُوا بِهَا); this directly ties the section's camel to divine sending and the community's transgression. | terra: God gives Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wrong her; divine giving and human violation are stated together before punishment.
terra: The challengers demand that the Messenger make a spring "تُفَجِّرَ لَنَا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ"; it is a direct Quranic use of f-j-r for water breaking out of ground.
terra: They demand a palm-and-grape garden with rivers made to gush through it abundantly; the root's bursting sense here produces the cultivated field developed in the section.
terra: God raises the sleepers, "ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَاهُمْ," after their long stillness; the explicit raiser and passive awakening preserve the agency contrast with 91:12.
terra: Each garden gives full produce and God makes a river burst through them, "وَفَجَّرْنَا خِلَالَهُمَا نَهَرًا"; f-j-r here sustains measured fertility.

terra: A believer rebukes his companion for denying the One who created him from dust and a drop, then "سَوَّاكَ رَجُلًا"; human taswiya becomes a moral argument against the owner's corrupt use of his garden.
terra: The flourishing garden may become "صَعِيدًا زَلَقًا," bare slippery ground; this is a direct reversal from cultivated estate to leveled, unproductive land.
terra: Its water may become sunken beyond recovery, showing the withheld-provision side of the water whose measured availability Thamud violated.
terra: The fruit is encompassed and the trellises collapse, making a built and cultivated estate share one destructive consequence.
luna: Rain brings forth vegetation that later becomes dry fragments scattered by wind (هَشِيمًا تَذْرُوهُ الرِّيَاحُ); this is another concrete version of the section's watered field becoming barren.
terra: Mountains are removed and the earth appears exposed at gathering, supplying a judgment scene in which all raised structures and relief vanish.

luna: The record omits neither small nor great deed (لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةً وَلَا كَبِيرَةً); this gives the section's image of each transgressor receiving a measured share the form of a complete account.

terra: The barrier-builder fills the gap until "سَاوَىٰ بَيْنَ الصَّدَفَيْنِ," making the structure level with the two cliffs; this different root-sense shows leveling as deliberate construction rather than destruction.
terra: Earth is made a cradle with paths, and water from heaven brings out paired plants; this gathers spread ground, guidance, rain, and cultivated growth.
terra: People eat and pasture their livestock from the plants of 20:53, completing the section's relation between field, provision, and animal.
terra: The question about the mountains is answered by their being blown away; it supplies the object and action whose level-plain result appears in 20:106-107.
terra: After the mountains are scattered, God leaves the earth "قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا," a bare level plain; this is the physical result invoked by the section's destructive taswiya.
terra: No crookedness or rise remains in that plain, completing the exact flattening scene of 20:106.
terra: "وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ" compresses the section's two linked terms: restraint determines what follows.

terra: The warned parties will know who follows "الصِّرَاطِ السَّوِيِّ"; the root here marks the even or right road, clarifying the section's claim that Thamud chose the wrong way from a fitted order.
terra: God creates night and day, sun and moon, each swimming in an orbit; the four actors of the surah's opening remain within one ordered motion.

luna: The dry earth stirs and swells after rain; it offers a specific barren-to-living ground parallel to the section's field, though the verse uses it as a resurrection sign. | terra: A lifeless earth stirs, swells, and grows after rain; the revival is the specific reverse of the field made barren by Thamud's act and punishment.
luna: God calls camels among His rites and commands His name over them at sacrifice; this contrasts an authorized, grateful offering with Thamud's forbidden destruction of God's sign.
luna: The ayah says neither camel flesh nor blood reaches God, but piety does (وَلَٰكِنْ يَنَالُهُ التَّقْوَىٰ مِنْكُمْ); it makes the section's restraint behind bodily acts explicit.
luna: The verse describes a town collapsed on its roofs and lofty palaces abandoned; that is a close physical parallel to Thamud's flattened settlement, though the people are unnamed here.
terra: Water descends "بِقَدَرٍ," is lodged in earth, and can be taken away; measure, hidden provision, and irreversible loss all bear on the violated drinking share.
terra: The measured stored water produces gardens of palms and grapes, giving the flourishing field made possible by the order in 23:18.

luna: Night and day are made to succeed one another (خِلْفَةً) for remembrance and gratitude; this directly connects the section's closing turn of night and day with recurring succession. | terra: God makes night and day "خِلْفَةً," successors to one another; this directly supports the source section's reading of the close as a final turn after which no counter-turn comes.
terra: Thamud deny the messengers, beginning the fuller version of the scene whose messenger, restraint, camel, and punishment follow.
terra: Salih commands his people to practice taqwa; this is the messenger's restraining word directly opposed to the later obedience of transgressors.
terra: Salih identifies himself as a trustworthy messenger, clarifying the divinely commissioned side of the section's messenger versus self-launched culprit contrast.
terra: Thamud are pictured amid "جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ"; together with the crops, palms, and carved houses in 26:148-149, it supplies the flourishing field that their act will destroy.

luna: The verse names palms whose fruit is heavy (طَلْعُهَا هَضِيمٌ); that fruitful palm is a specific reversal of the section's secondary reading of ʿaqr as cutting a palm's head so it will not bear. | terra: "وَزُرُوعٍ وَنَخْلٍ" gives the crops and palms whose flourishing heads make the source section's barren-field and severed-palm senses of ʿaqr perceptible.

luna: The same Thamud passage says they skillfully hew houses from mountains (تَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا); this complements the section's palaces on the plain with their mountain dwellings. | terra: Their confident carving of mountain homes completes the cultivated-land scene of 26:147-148 and anticipates the leveling of the civilization built upon it.
terra: Salih again commands taqwa and obedience immediately before forbidding obedience to the extravagant in 26:151; the two imperatives mark the opposed authorities.
terra: Salih forbids obedience to "أَمْرَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ," those who exceed bounds; it identifies the social command opposite the messenger's restraining warning.
terra: Those leaders corrupt the earth and do not set things right; the statement carries the section's inward breach into ruined land and order.

luna: Salih assigns the she-camel a drink and the people a known day's drink (شِرْبٌ مَعْلُومٌ); this makes the violated water share in the section concrete and apportioned. | terra: "لَهَا شِرْبٌ وَلَكُمْ شِرْبُ يَوْمٍ مَّعْلُومٍ" states the camel's and people's measured turns at water, the exact quota whose breach the section connects to their own allotted return.

luna: The messenger explicitly forbids harming the camel and warns of punishment; the ayah supplies the boundary the people choose to cross. | terra: Salih forbids touching the camel with harm and warns of a tremendous day's punishment, binding the protected animal directly to consequence.

luna: The people hamstring the camel (فَعَقَرُوهَا) and regret it; this is the act and immediate human response behind the section's account of a transgression. | terra: They hamstring her and become regretful; the physical cut immediately begins the moral aftermath developed by the section.

luna: Its contribution is the punishment that follows their camel-killing, completing the prior ayah's image of regret with the consequence. | terra: The punishment seizes them, completing the hamstringing scene and showing the consequence following the deed.
terra: God sends Salih to Thamud, who split into two contending groups; divine mission and the community's own divergent movement appear together.
terra: Salih asks why they seek to hasten evil before good and calls them to forgiveness, exposing their self-propelled rush toward the consequence of 27:51.
terra: Nine men in the city corrupt the land and do not reform; this collective background makes the section's single self-launched wretch part of an organized breach.
terra: They swear to attack Salih and his family by night, making night itself the cover for their transgression before their plan returns upon them.
terra: They devise a plan and God devises while they do not perceive; the reversal prepares the irreversible outcome named in 27:51.
terra: The command to see "عَاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ" ends with God destroying the Thamud plotters and their people together; it is the exact aftermath the section locates behind the struck animal.

luna: The verse names Thamud's houses fallen in ruin because of their wrongdoing (فَتِلْكَ بُيُوتُهُمْ خَاوِيَةً بِمَا ظَلَمُوا); it directly joins their guilt to the collapse of their built place. | terra: "فَتِلْكَ بُيُوتُهُمْ خَاوِيَةً بِمَا ظَلَمُوا" leaves their houses empty because of wrongdoing, concretely completing the destruction announced in 27:51.

luna: Those who believed and were mindful are saved; this adjacent outcome completes the ruin of Thamud with the contrasting field of protection. | terra: God saves those who believed and "كَانُوا يَتَّقُونَ" beside the ruined houses of 27:52; taqwa functions as the protection the transgressors tore away.
terra: The command to travel and see the criminals' "عَاقِبَةُ" turns ruined places into evidence of the aftermath the section locates in Thamud's houses.
luna: God does not destroy a town before sending a messenger to recite His signs; this states the divine order of messenger-before-judgment that the section sees in Salih's mission to Thamud.
terra: The question of an unbroken night asks who besides God could bring light; by suspending alternation, it exposes how much the section's ordered watch depends on a divinely set boundary.
terra: The matching question of an unbroken day asks who could bring night for rest; it is the converse boundary to 28:71 and clarifies the normal succession evoked by the section.
terra: The final home is for those who do not seek elevation or corruption on earth, and "الْعَاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ"; it reverses Thamud's proud building and earthly فساد.

luna: Each people is seized for its sin (بِذَنْبِهِ); the different fates include storm, cry, earth-swallowing, and drowning, making the section's sin-and-measured-consequence relation concrete. | terra: "فَكُلًّا أَخَذْنَا بِذَنبِهِ" makes each community's destructive seizure follow its own sin, directly matching the section's rear/act/consequence meeting.
luna: Punishment covers people from above and beneath their feet (يَغْشَاهُمُ الْعَذَابُ); this makes the section's judgment closing over Thamud like night explicit.
terra: Former peoples cultivated earth and built it more greatly, yet their outcome followed rejection of messengers; this directly joins construction, field, mission, and aftermath.
terra: The evildoers' "عَاقِبَةَ" is the worst because they deny God's signs; consequence follows denial with the same logic as the Thamud close.
terra: Corruption appears on land and sea because of what people's hands earn so that they taste part of what they did; inward breach becomes environmental disorder and measured consequence.
terra: A day comes "لَا مَرَدَّ لَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ"; the absence of any repelling turn directly illuminates the section's claim that final judgment has no successor to undo it.
terra: God "سَوَّاهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِهِ" forms the human and breathes spirit into him, making the inward self the third constructed dwelling described by the section.

luna: The one who purifies himself does so for his own soul (وَمَنْ تَزَكَّىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَتَزَكَّىٰ لِنَفْسِهِ); this repeats the section's purification root, though in a statement about personal benefit. | terra: Whoever purifies himself "فَإِنَّمَا يَتَزَكَّىٰ لِنَفْسِهِ" and the journey ends with God; the soul both receives the cultivation and bears its outcome.
terra: Travelers are asked to see the outcome of peoples stronger than themselves; vanished power and earthworks illuminate the fate of Thamud's confident architecture.
terra: A dead land is revived and grain is brought from it; it directly supplies the section's field as an image of what is cultivated rather than buried.
terra: Gardens are planted and springs are made to burst, "وَفَجَّرْنَا فِيهَا مِنَ الْعُيُونِ"; f-j-r here creates the watered field rather than a moral flood.
terra: People eat the fruit of the revived, irrigated ground; this states the provision produced by the bursting springs in 36:34.

luna: The verse describes night as a sign from which daylight is stripped away; this is a close reverse view of the section's day opening and night covering. | terra: Night is a sign from which God strips daylight, leaving darkness; the stripping image closely matches the section's reciprocal covering and uncovering.

luna: The sun runs to its appointed course; its assigned motion supports the section's opening picture of each body keeping its place. | terra: The sun runs to its appointed station, expressing the exact placement and ordered movement with which the section opens.

luna: The moon is assigned its phases; this contributes the ordered lunar following that the section sets beside the sun and day. | terra: The moon is measured through stages until it returns like an old palm stalk, joining measured succession with the palm-field imagery developed in the section.

luna: Neither sun overtakes the moon nor night outstrips day, each moving in an orbit (كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ); this states the ordered alternation at the beginning of the section. | terra: Neither sun overtakes moon nor night precedes day; the cosmic boundary makes the section's contrast with the soul that breaks its limit especially clear.
terra: The ayah explicitly opposes "الْمُتَّقِينَ" and "الْفُجَّارِ"; it is the clearest external pairing of the two inward portions named together in 91:8.
terra: The repeated Adam scene again joins divine taswiya with the breathing of spirit, reinforcing the section's constructive use of the root for the human self.

luna: God wraps night over day and day over night (يُكَوِّرُ اللَّيْلَ عَلَى النَّهَارِ); this is the ordered covering and uncovering against which the section sets the soul's breach of restraint. | terra: God wraps night over day and day over night while sun and moon run to fixed terms; the reciprocal wrapping is the ordered succession that the final irreversible judgment ends.

terra: Water descends, travels as springs within earth, raises varied crops, then leaves them yellow debris; the whole measured passage from hidden water to growth and waste parallels the section's field movement.
terra: The condemned person can only "يَتَّقِي بِوَجْهِهِ" the punishment; this desperate bodily shielding reverses the sound protective cover of taqwa developed in the section.
terra: Earlier peoples were stronger and left greater traces in the earth, yet God seized them "بِذُنُوبِهِمْ"; built landscape and sin's aftermath are explicitly joined.
terra: Earlier peoples are seized because of their sins after their messengers bring clear proofs, completing 40:21's built-earth traces with messenger, denial, and consequence.
terra: God makes earth a settlement and sky a structure, forms people well, and provides good things; built cosmos, human formation, and provision appear as one ordered home.
terra: The command to see former peoples' outcome notes their greater numbers, strength, and traces on earth; their works could not protect them from consequence.
terra: God places sustenance in the earth and measures it in four days "سَوَاءً لِّلسَّائِلِينَ"; equal provision and measured earth illuminate the camel's apportioned water.
terra: God turns to the smoke-like heaven and commands heaven and earth to come willingly, placing both structures under a single ordering command.
terra: God completes the heavens as seven and assigns each its command, continuing 41:11 with the precise cosmic fitting that the section transfers to the soul.

luna: Thamud are shown the way but choose blindness over guidance, then the humiliating thunderbolt seizes them; this states the section's wrong choice and its consequence in another account of the same people. | terra: Thamud are guided but prefer blindness, so humiliating punishment seizes them for what they earned; wrong choice and its following consequence are stated together.
terra: Believers who practiced taqwa are saved beside Thamud's seizure in 41:17, making restraint the protective opposite of their chosen blindness.
luna: The earth is humbled and then stirs after rain; this repeats the dry-to-fruitful land boundary in the section, here as a sign of resurrection.
terra: A calamity comes from what people's hands have earned, while much is pardoned; this states the act-to-aftermath relation with an explicit boundary against imagining automatic total requital.
terra: The same warning names a day from God for which there is no repelling; it restates the terminal, unreversible turn developed at the section's close.
terra: The command to see earlier peoples' outcome states that God destroyed them; the visible ruined-land formulation closely matches the section's leveled houses.
terra: Those who accept guidance receive more guidance and God "آتَاهُمْ تَقْوَاهُمْ"; this closely echoes the soul being given its taqwa while stressing the guided reception of it.
terra: The sky above is built and adorned "without any rifts"; its unbroken construction gives a specific cosmic boundary against which the section's rupture image can be seen.
terra: The earth is spread, stabilized, and made to grow beautiful kinds, continuing the intact sky of 50:6 into the section's ordered and cultivated ground.
terra: Blessed water descends and grows gardens and harvested grain, directly joining sky-water, worked earth, and crop.
terra: Tall palms with layered clusters display the intact, fruitful palm-head that the source section's secondary ʿaqr sense places under threat.
terra: The crop is provision, and dead land is revived by rain; this states the life-bearing outcome opposite the section's barren field.
terra: Thamud are granted enjoyment only for a time, giving their prosperity an explicitly measured limit before the blast.
terra: They defy their Lord's command, so the thunderbolt seizes them while they look; broken restraint and immediate consequence meet.
terra: After one man rose to attack the camel, the punished people cannot rise and receive no help; their inability to stand is a pointed reversal of the section's self-launching image.
terra: God builds heaven with power and expands it; this directly repeats the built-sky pole of the section's taswiya meeting.
terra: God spreads the earth as an excellent preparer, completing the heaven-and-spread-earth pair begun in 51:47.

terra: The wrongdoers have a "ذَنُوبًا" like their companions' portion; this Quranic share-word, with its bucket background identified by the source section, makes punishment an allotted draw related to ذنب.
terra: The promised punishment is declared certain to occur; 52:8 supplies its lack of any repeller, matching the section's finality.
terra: "مَا لَهُ مِن دَافِعٍ" states directly that nothing can push the punishment away once it comes.
terra: God leaves nothing of Thamud remaining; the terse statement reinforces the total, unreversed finality developed at the section's close.
luna: The sky's gates open with pouring water (بِمَاءٍ مُنْهَمِرٍ); this preceding ayah supplies the flood's rain source before the next verse's earth springs.

luna: The earth is made to burst into springs (وَفَجَّرْنَا الْأَرْضَ عُيُونًا) as floodwater meets the rain; it supplies the section's image of a burst that overflows its bounds. | terra: God makes the earth burst into springs, "وَفَجَّرْنَا الْأَرْضَ عُيُونًا," and the waters meet according to a matter already measured; this gathers the section's rupture, earth, water, meeting, and measure.

luna: God says He is sending the she-camel as a trial (فِتْنَةً لَهُمْ), matching the section's camel as a divine sending and test of restraint. | terra: "إِنَّا مُرْسِلُو النَّاقَةِ فِتْنَةً لَّهُمْ" explicitly makes God the sender of the she-camel, sharpening the section's contrast with the man who sends himself toward her.

luna: The water is divided between them (الْمَاءُ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ), giving the section's camel and people distinct measured shares. | terra: The water is "قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ" and every drink has its turn; it supplies the measured water-share that the source section says Thamud violated, while 54:29 supplies the attack.

luna: They call their companion, who then hamstrings the camel (فَنَادَوْا صَاحِبَهُمْ ... فَعَقَرَ); the act is initiated by the people, as the section says the rebel sends himself into action. | terra: They call their companion, and "فَتَعَاطَىٰ فَعَقَرَ"; this is the parallel scene in which one man undertakes the act and hamstrings the camel after the apportioned drink of 54:28.

luna: The question about the punishment and warnings follows the hamstringing, so this ayah contributes the announced consequence to the water-share scene. | terra: The question "how were My punishment and warnings?" makes the consequence of the self-initiated hamstringing in 54:29 explicit before 54:31 depicts the remains.

luna: One blast turns them into dry fragments like a fence-maker's brushwood (كَأَنَّهُمْ هَشِيمُ الْمُحْتَظِرِ); it connects the people's ruin with the section's field made barren and structures flattened. | terra: One blast leaves them like the dry crushed material of a pen, converting a living herd-and-field setting into flattened plant debris.
terra: A settled punishment reaches Lot's people in the early morning, another specific scene in which the ordinary night-day turn becomes terminal judgment.
terra: The sun and moon move "بِحُسْبَانٍ," by calculation; this supplies the measured cosmic order that the section carries into the soul and its allotted consequences.
terra: God raises the sky and sets the balance; the source section likewise makes the built sky the model for a soul set in order.
terra: "أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا فِي الْمِيزَانِ" turns cosmic balance into a ban on transgression, exactly the section's move from ordered heavens to Thamud's tughyan.
terra: The command to uphold weight justly and not diminish the balance illuminates the violated water-share and the exactly measured return described in the section.
luna: The verse asks what people sow (مَا تَحْرُثُونَ), directly naming the plowed field that the section uses to figure what grows from the soul.
luna: It asks whether people or God make the seed grow; this makes the field's fruitfulness in the section an outcome of divine measure, not self-sufficiency.
luna: God could make the crop dry fragments (حُطَامًا); the possible harvest turned barren directly mirrors the section's growing field and cut or buried field.

luna: A wall with a gate separates believers from hypocrites at the final judgment (بَيْنَهُم بِسُورٍ لَّهُ بَابٌ); it develops the section's taqwa-as-boundary image into a last separation between two outcomes.
terra: A people who thought their fortresses would protect them have their houses ruined by their own hands and believers' hands; built security becomes the instrument and site of consequence.
terra: Those who practice taqwa are told that every soul must look at what it has sent ahead for tomorrow; inward restraint is joined directly to the consequence following one's act.
terra: God is the one who "بَعَثَ فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ رَسُولًا" who purifies them; it makes explicit both sides of the section's sent-messenger versus self-launched sinner meeting.
terra: Whoever practices taqwa receives a way out, making restraint itself a protecting boundary rather than the breached cover of fujur.
terra: God provides unexpectedly and has set a measure for everything; this completes 65:2 by joining taqwa, provision, and measure.
terra: The seven heavens are layered without disparity in the Merciful's creation; this intact cosmic fitting is the direct opposite of the breach and overflow that the section carries into the soul.
terra: Repeated sight returns unable to find a flaw in the heavens of 67:3, sharpening the contrast between cosmic order and a soul that tears its proper boundary.
terra: The garden owners swear they will cut its crop in the morning; this supplies the intended severing whose nocturnal reversal appears in 68:19-20.
terra: They make no exception to their plan, exposing the false confidence that no counter-turn will intervene before the night's judgment.
terra: A visitation from the Lord circles the garden while its owners sleep, linking night-cover with an irreversible field judgment.
terra: By morning the garden is "كَالصَّرِيمِ," stripped or darkened; the ayah meets the section's night, severing, and barren-field images at once.
terra: "فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطَّاغِيَةِ" makes Thamud's destruction arrive through an overwhelming event named from the same transgressive field as their tughyan.
terra: Earth and mountains are lifted and crushed in one crushing, a direct large-scale parallel to the section's destructive leveling.
terra: God is able "عَلَىٰ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ" even to fashion fingertips at resurrection; constructive taswiya reaches the body's smallest detail and counters the flattening sense.
terra: "بَلْ يُرِيدُ الْإِنسَانُ لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ" presents fujur as a person's forward-projecting intention; it matches the section's inward tearing that releases a self-propelled transgression.
terra: From a clinging form God creates and "فَسَوَّىٰ" the human; the embryonic context supplies another bodily sense of completion behind the section's fashioned soul.

luna: Humanity is shown the path and may be grateful or ungrateful (إِمَّا شَاكِرًا وَإِمَّا كَفُورًا); this directly articulates the two moral possibilities that the section gives the soul. | terra: God guides the human to the way, whether grateful or ungrateful; the two possible responses parallel the soul's given capacities without using the section's field imagery.
terra: God's servants drink from a spring that they make gush abundantly, "يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيرًا"; the controlled opening contrasts with fujur as uncontrolled inward overflow.
terra: The earth is made a resting spread, a concise parallel to the section's laid-out ground between formation and destruction.
terra: Mountains serve as pegs for the spread earth of 78:6, adding the stability that the later leveling scene removes.
terra: God makes night a garment, directly joining the cosmic covering of night to the section's developed clothing sense of taqwa.
terra: Day is made the time of livelihood, so the removal of night's garment yields provision in the ordered succession described by the section.

luna: The passage asks whether creating heaven or people is harder, then says God built it; this begins the same heaven-to-earth construction sequence that echoes the section's created order. | terra: "أَمِ السَّمَاءُ بَنَاهَا" begins a creation sequence that parallels the section's built sky; 79:28 specifies its taswiya and 79:30 the spread earth.

luna: God raises heaven's ceiling and proportions it (فَسَوَّاهَا), repeating the sawwā of the section's formed sky and setting up its contrast with Thamud's leveling. | terra: God raises the sky's canopy and "فَسَوَّاهَا"; this is the direct constructive use of the same verb that the section sets against Thamud's leveling.

luna: This next ayah darkens heaven's night and brings out its morning; it supplies the ordered covering and opening that follows the fashioned sky. | terra: God darkens its night and brings out its morning brightness, restaging the orderly covering and opening at the start of surah 91.

luna: The earth is spread out (دَحَاهَا), a direct parallel in image to the section's spread ground between sky and soul and its plain made level. | terra: "وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ دَحَاهَا" supplies the spread earth that stands between the section's formed heavens and leveled people.

luna: The following verse brings water and pasture out of the earth; it makes the fertile ground in the section dependent on provision from above. | terra: The spread earth yields its water and pasture, joining rain, ground, and growth within the same creation sequence.
terra: The mountains are fixed in place; this continues the ordered earth scene of 79:30-31 and marks the stability opposite Thamud's ruined built landscape.

luna: Pasture is made provision for people and their cattle (مَتَاعًا لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ), completing the prior water-and-ground scene with its herds. | terra: "مَتَاعًا لَّكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ" makes earth's growth provision for people and livestock, including the animal-world dimension of the section's camel and pasture.

luna: The one who transgresses (طَغَىٰ) is set against the one who restrains himself in the next passage; this same limit-crossing marks Thamud's wrong course in the section. | terra: "فَأَمَّا مَن طَغَىٰ" begins the moral choice with transgression, linking the creation sequence of 79:27-33 to the same inward disorder as Thamud.
terra: Preferring the nearer life states what the transgressor of 79:37 chooses before the contrasting restraint in 79:40.

luna: The one who fears standing before his Lord and restrains the soul from desire (وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوَىٰ) enacts taqwa as a bridle, directly opposite the soul's unleashed fujūr. | terra: One who fears standing before the Lord "وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوَىٰ" restrains the soul, the clearest nonlexical parallel to taqwa as a dam holding back overflow.

luna: The garden is the refuge of the restrained person; this next ayah completes the preceding inward restraint with its opposite outcome to transgression. | terra: The garden is the refuge of the self-restraining person, completing the cultivated-field outcome opposite transgression.

luna: God pours water abundantly (أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا الْمَاءَ صَبًّا); this begins the rain-to-field sequence behind the section's fertile plain. | terra: Water is poured abundantly before the earth is split and grain grown; it begins the rain-to-field sequence implicit in the section's cultivated earth.

luna: The earth is split open (ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا), followed by crops; the ayah gives the broken soil from which a living field emerges. | terra: "ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا" makes the field's rupture productive, a precise contrast to the inward rupture that releases fujur.

luna: Grain is brought forth from that split earth (فَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا حَبًّا); it supplies the crop-growth side of the section's contrast with barren ground. | terra: God grows grain in the opened earth, completing the productive breach of 80:26.

luna: Fruit and pasture appear in the same sequence; this ayah contributes the cultivated and grazed yield of the land. | terra: Fruit and pasture extend the crop sequence and connect the opened ground to both people and grazing animals.

luna: That produce is provision for people and livestock (مَتَاعًا لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ), completing the rain, soil, and crop relation that the section places under divine provision. | terra: The growth is provision for people and their livestock, identifying what the rightly opened and watered earth yields.

luna: The girl buried alive (الْمَوْءُودَةُ) is the opposite agent and victim from the soul that buries itself in the section; the parallel makes moral burial a question of responsibility, not just concealment.
luna: The next ayah asks for what sin she was killed (بِأَيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ); it completes that reversal by exposing the buried victim's innocence rather than blaming her.
luna: After the upheaval of sky and earth, every soul knows what it has brought (عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَا أَحْضَرَتْ); this makes the section's final, irreversible reckoning of the soul explicit.
luna: The night is sworn by as it recedes (وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا عَسْعَسَ); the next dawn verse completes the section's night-to-opening transition.
luna: Dawn is described as breathing (وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ) after the night recedes in 81:17; this gives a close image of night giving way to opening light.
terra: The sky splitting open at judgment turns the section's constructive sky into a breached one; it also prepares the seas' bursting in 82:3.
terra: When the seas "فُجِّرَتْ," a cosmic boundary bursts at judgment; this gives the section's water-breach sense its largest destructive scale.

luna: God creates, fashions, and proportions the human being (خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ); the same sawwā root links a formed creature with the section's fashioned sky and leveled settlement. | terra: God "خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ" creates, completes, and balances the human; it is the closest external formulation of the soul/body being fitted like the built sky.

luna: The righteous are in bliss (إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ); this gives the good side of the moral division whose next ayah names the wicked. | terra: The righteous are in bliss, forming the positive half of the immediate two-outcome contrast whose fujjar half appears in 82:14.

luna: The wicked (الْفُجَّارَ) are in Hell, using the section's fujūr word for the contrary moral course and its consequence. | terra: "وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ لَفِي جَحِيمٍ" gives fujur its opposed final field beside the righteous outcome in 82:13.
luna: The record of the wicked (كِتَابَ الْفُجَّارِ) is placed in Sijjīn; this repeats the section's fujūr category and gives its morally buried course a recorded destination.

luna: This verse says people's earnings have left rust over their hearts (رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِم); it contrasts the section's torn protective veil with a covering produced by sin that instead obscures the inner self. | terra: What people earn lays a rust "رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِم"; this is a pointed reversal of the section's imagery, because tearing the protective cover through fujur produces a corrupt covering over the heart.

luna: God created and proportioned (خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ); this repeats the section's sawwā for formed creation before it turns to what grows and withers. | terra: "الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ" makes taswiya the completion and fitting of creation, the constructive pole of the section's final word-meeting.

luna: God measures and guides (قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ); in this sequence it contributes the measured order that precedes pasture and its fate. | terra: "وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ" places measure and guidance immediately after creative taswiya, clarifying why violated measure is also a wrong path in the section.

luna: God brings out pasture (أَخْرَجَ الْمَرْعَىٰ), the living field side of the section's ground and crop image. | terra: God "أَخْرَجَ الْمَرْعَىٰ," bringing out pasture after creation and measure; it supplies the living field attached to the section's spread land.

luna: The pasture becomes dark stubble (غُثَاءً أَحْوَىٰ); this gives a precise grown-then-spent counterpart to the section's field made barren. | terra: God then makes pasture dark stubble, "غُثَاءً أَحْوَىٰ"; this reversal from growth to waste illuminates the section's cultivated field turned barren.

luna: The verse says the one who purifies himself succeeds (قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّىٰ), closely restating the purifying path and outcome of the section. | terra: "قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ" almost restates 91:9, confirming cultivation or purification of the self as the successful field opposed to burial.

luna: The verse asks people to consider how camels were created (إِلَى الْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ); this places the divinely formed animal at the center of a created order that the section shows Thamud violating.
luna: The next ayah asks how the sky was raised (السَّمَاءِ كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ); it contributes the section's sky image to the same passage that begins with the camel.
luna: The passage next asks how mountains were set firm (الْجِبَالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ); it places fixed terrain between the camel and the spread earth in the linked creation survey.
luna: The earth is described as spread out (الْأَرْضِ كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ); this completes that camel-to-sky-to-land sequence with the section's ground image.

luna: The oath is by dawn (وَالْفَجْرِ), the same named word-family the section connects to fujūr's image of a split opening in the night. | terra: The oath "وَالْفَجْرِ" places the dawn itself before the reader, the light-bearing rupture from which the source section begins its f-j-r meeting.

luna: Thamud are recalled as cutting into rock in a valley (بِالْوَادِ), adding another account of their built landscape to the section's plain and palaces. | terra: Thamud carve rock in the valley; the verse supplies the built landscape that the source section imagines returned to a flattened plain.
terra: The peoples just named "طَغَوْا فِي الْبِلَادِ"; it explicitly connects Thamud's landscape to the transgression that upsets the section's measured order.
terra: They multiply corruption in the lands, showing the outward spread of the inward fujur and tughyan described in the section.
terra: God pours upon them a scourge of punishment; "فَصَبَّ" reverses the section's life-giving water into a measured destructive outpouring.
terra: "Your Lord is ever watchful" closes the sequence of transgression, corruption, and poured punishment, reinforcing the section's divine stance beyond fear of any counter-consequence.
terra: The earth is crushed repeatedly at judgment, extending the section's leveled plain from one people to the final scene.

luna: God guides the human being to the two paths (وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ), a direct formulation of choosing between the two courses in the section. | terra: "وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ" gives the human two evident ways, a concise parallel to the soul receiving two opposed directions and then choosing.

luna: The verse repeats the night-covering formula (وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ), directly echoing the section's night that covers in its appointed turn. | terra: The oath by night "when it covers" repeats the exact opening action of surah 91 and begins another movement from cosmic alternation to unlike moral efforts.

luna: Day is sworn by as it appears (وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ); this gives the opening of light that complements the preceding covering night. | terra: The oath by day "when it manifests" supplies the answering uncovering to 92:1, matching the section's orderly opening after cover.

luna: Human endeavors are diverse (إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ); this bridges the paired night and day to the two diverging courses of the section. | terra: "Your efforts are diverse" carries the paired night and day of 92:1-2 into opposed human courses, the same cosmic-to-inward movement developed in the section.

luna: The giving person who fears God (أَعْطَىٰ وَاتَّقَىٰ) follows the section's God-conscious and successful path. | terra: Giving and "وَاتَّقَىٰ" begin one of two inward courses, closely paralleling the section's paired portions and fields.
luna: Affirming the best completes the description of the good course begun in the prior ayah, before its promised ease.

luna: God promises to ease the God-conscious giver toward ease (فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ), closely matching the section's promise attached to its successful path. | terra: God eases the giving, Godfearing person toward ease; the result shows one course of the soul becoming a fitted path.

luna: The withholding, self-sufficient person begins the opposite course; this contributes the section's buried and unsuccessful field. | terra: The miser who deems himself self-sufficient begins the opposite course to 92:5, a specific moral reversal rather than merely another outcome.
luna: Denial of the best completes the rejecting course described in the preceding ayah, matching the section's denial of the messenger.

luna: The opposite person is eased toward hardship (فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ); it gives a paired contrary outcome to the section's successful course. | terra: God eases that person toward hardship, completing the two-path consequence that the section pictures as two fields.
luna: Only the most wretched (الْأَشْقَى) enters the fire; the same distinctive word links the self-starting worst man in the section to the consequence of that course.
luna: This person denied the truth and turned away (كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ), which parallels Thamud's denial of their messenger and their refusal of the sign.
luna: The most God-conscious (الْأَتْقَى) is kept away from that fire, setting the section's protected, restrained path against the most wretched one.
luna: The person gives wealth to purify himself (يُؤْتِي مَالَهُ يَتَزَكَّىٰ), supplying another concrete Qur'anic formulation of the section's purifying course.
terra: The oath by morning brightness names the illuminated side of the dawn meeting, while 93:2 gives its nocturnal counterpart.
terra: Night when it grows still supplies a peaceful form of covering beside 93:1, a boundary-preserving contrast to the section's inward overflow.
terra: "إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَيَطْغَىٰ" locates the overflow in the human being, closely matching the section's movement from cosmic order into inward transgression.
terra: The human transgresses upon seeing himself self-sufficient; this gives the self-launching breach in 96:6 a specific inward cause.
terra: The night of decree remains peace "حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ"; dawn is the appointed boundary that ends a night, reinforcing the section's orderly turn rather than a lawless breach.
luna: Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it; this is the good portion in the section's paired moral outcomes.

luna: Whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it; the next ayah completes the exact balancing of outcome that the section associates with the camel's allotted share and the people's consequence.
